speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Defence what are the current guidelines for standards relating to full-time National Servicemen's accommodation in camps in terms of (i) the number of occupants per room (ii) the number of occupants per floor (iii) the amount of living space per occupant in terms of square metres, excluding shared living facilities (iv) ventilation requirements and (v) the ratio of occupants to available toilets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: The rooms are designed to make good use of natural ventilation and daylight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Typically, a four-person room has two ceiling fans and larger rooms may have more fans installed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just ask Senior Minister of State how new are these guidelines, whether they have been revised during COVID-19 to take into account the infection measures?

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: As I alluded to in my answer, our norms are developed in compliance with national regulations.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: So, every time that there will be improvements or changes to these regulations, then certainly, we will take them in to make sure that we remain up-to-date in our provisions.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: In terms of the improvements or adjustments that we have made to render our facilities more pandemic-ready, that too has been made.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: For continued operational readiness and effectiveness, the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF)/SAF buildings and infrastructure must be pandemic-ready.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: In new projects or when existing infrastructure is refreshed, a key design consideration is flexibility to allow for adaptation to dynamic requirements.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Among the considerations to ensure pandemic-readiness are: one, space planning for safe social distancing for crowd and transmission control; two, provisions for plexiglass or shield equivalence as separators; and three, anti-microbial coatings on common touchpoints.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Natural ventilation is a key design consideration for MINDEF/SAF accommodation spaces.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: In the event of outbreaks, MINDEF/SAF also has protocols, such as: one, demarcating ring-fencing facilities; two, instituting isolation plans; and three, implementing medical plans to deal with the potential emergence of clusters.
